# Ket: parametric CAD for agents

Ket is a parametric CAD and PCB tool that you drive with
tools. The design is a JSON document: parameters, an ordered list of named
features, and checks. Geometry is rebuilt from it by OpenCascade every time
it changes, so every dimension can be an expression over parameters.

## Coordinates
- Millimetres and degrees. Z is up. The XY plane at z=0 is the build plate.
- box is centered on X/Y and sits on z=0 by default; cylinder starts at the
  origin and grows along +axis.

## Projects and tabs
- Each open project is a tab in the user's Ket window; several can be open
  at once. Over MCP, open_project opens one (activate: false keeps the
  user's current tab), close_project closes it, and commands on a closed
  project open it in a background tab by themselves.

## Workflow
1. get_document to see what exists. If the project is new, set_description
   with the brief.
2. set_parameters for every dimension that matters (sizes, wall, clearances,
   hole positions). Derive the rest: case_w = "board_w + 2*wall + 2*gap".
3. set_checks for the requirements (fits, clearances, minimum walls) before
   modelling, so you can verify instead of guess.
4. Model with features, in a few calls: primitives and extrusions, then
   boolean (cut/union), then shell, then fillet/chamfer last.
5. run_checks after each group of changes. Fix every failed feature and
   failed check before continuing. Read warnings: a cut that removes nothing
   is a misplaced tool.
6. render (iso + another view) to look at the result when it matters, or
   section to see inside. Compare the picture with the intent.
7. Summarize for the user in a few lines.

## AI-first diagnose and repair
- Start with get_document and get_problems. The latter combines history,
  CAD checks, PCB DRC/connectivity, electrical rules and manufacturing
  warnings with stable problem IDs, objects, locations and fix guidance.
- Read get_board/get_copper for exact PCB objects. Diagnose from evidence;
  never declare a board electrically safe just because geometry passes.
- Use preview_changes with a small batch before a risky repair. It prepares
  dependent steps in order, builds the candidate and reports introduced,
  resolved and remaining problems WITHOUT saving anything. Apply reviewed
  steps with batch or on a proposal. Preview does not certify the circuit.
- edit_copper repairs specific numbered tracks/vias without rerouting a
  whole net. Numbers belong to the current revision; re-read after removals
  or autoroute. move_component unroute: true remains safer for moved parts.
- Set pin intent with set_pin_rules from actual datasheets. run_erc checks
  declared output conflicts, no-connect and required pins; unknown types
  remain unverified. Do not guess types or weaken checks to get a pass.
- Re-run get_problems after each repair. Inspect renders and measured fits;
  focus_problem can show the user the current problem in the viewport.
- If history replay fails, edits and exports are blocked on the incomplete
  design. get_history shows the failed operation and last good sequence;
  use a compatible build or undo to that sequence, never silently skip it.
- cancel_operation interrupts local kernel work and queued calls, preserves
  saved operations and rebuilds. It does not stop a server AI conversation.
- Finish by naming remaining errors, untyped pins and manufacturer/physical
  checks that still need a human. Never claim upload, payment or DFM approval.

## Sketches
- For any outline that is not a plain box or cylinder, sketch it: sketch
  on a plane, then extrude or revolve with sketch: "<name>".
- add_to_sketch shapes (rect, circle, slot, polygon) come fully
  constrained; loops inside the outer loop become holes.
- Features on a body (a boss on a lid, a pocket in a wall): sketch with
  on: { feature, face: { where: ">Z" } } instead of computing the plane
  offset; it follows the body when parameters change. Extrude > 0 adds,
  < 0 makes a tool to cut with boolean. solve_sketch shows the frame.
- For custom outlines, give points (rough guesses are fine), lines/arcs that
  share points, and constraints (horizontal, vertical, length, distance,
  radius, tangent, ...). Drive values with parameters.
- solve_sketch after editing: aim for status "solved" with dof 0. A
  conflict names the constraint numbers to change.
- Revolve: draw the half cross-section on XZ on the +X side and revolve
  about Z.
- Loft blends between sections on parallel planes (rect base to round top);
  sweep moves a cross-section along a path of points with rounded corners
  (bend), for handles, channels and bent rods. Both need single loops: make
  hollow shapes by lofting/sweeping the inside too and cutting it.
- Symmetric parts: model one side, then mirror it (XZ for left/right).
  Repeat around an axis with pattern kind "polar" (spokes, bolt circles).
- Lettering that must exist in the part (raised, engraved): the text
  feature, then union or cut it.

- Gears: the gear command makes involute spur, helical, herringbone,
  internal, rack, worm and bevel gears. Place the first one; every other
  gear uses mesh: { with, angle } (or coaxial for a shared shaft), so
  centers and tooth phases are solved. Drive the whole train with one
  parameter in the first gear's rotation and check it with get_gears.
- Motion: Play advances the driven parameter (a gear train drives itself).
  set_motion adds joints for other moving bodies and physics for loose
  ones (balls, loads) that fall and collide; check with get_motion and
  simulate.
- Mechanisms: planetary picks tooth counts for a ratio and places sun,
  planets (they orbit), ring and carrier; cam (lift as an expression of t,
  follower joint kind "cam"), geneva (drive + wheel), belt (pulleys turn
  together). get_mechanisms for sizes and warnings.
- sweep_motion steps the motion and reports the first parameter value
  where moving parts collide; run it before calling a mechanism done.

## Appearance (display only)
- set_material from a preset (aluminum, brushed_steel, chrome, glass,
  rubber, wood, screen, ...) and assign_material to bodies. Materials are
  PBR: base color, metalness, roughness, plus texture maps (albedo, normal,
  roughness, metallic, ao, displacement) from procedural patterns, laid on
  with uv (box for any shape, cylindrical for round parts).
- add_decal / add_decals print text or images onto a body: labels, key
  legends, logos. Point normal out of the surface at at.
- Check with render shading: "realistic". Problems show as appearance_problems.
- For printed PCB lettering/logos use add_board_artwork instead of decals:
  decals are display-only and do not become manufacturing silkscreen.

## PCB
1. set_board with an outline (rect, or an XY sketch driven by the same
   parameters as the enclosure). The board becomes body "board" and each
   part "part_<REF>" in the 3D model.
2. find_parts by part number, part_info to see pins, add_component by LCSC
   number. Prefer JLCPCB basic parts in stock.
3. connect pins into nets by name ("U1.VIN", "J1.GND"); set_net_class for
   power nets (e.g. 0.5 mm).
4. Place parts with room to route: connectors at the edge, decoupling caps
   next to their pins. get_board shows sizes; run_drc catches overlaps.
   Moving a routed part: move_component with unroute: true, then
   autoroute and stitch_vias again.
5. autoroute, then run_drc. Fix violations, re-route if needed. To redo
   part of the board ("this area again, straighter/wider"), autoroute with
   region (or nets): only those nets are replaced. tidy_tracks straightens
   and widens existing tracks without rerouting (width for "thicker").
6. render_board to look at it; export_fab writes the JLCPCB package.
   manufacturing_quote is local preflight (not a live price quote);
   export_manufacturing adds board specs, check results and ordering notes
   for JLCPCB/PCBWay, without uploading, ordering or paying.
7. For an enclosure: model around "board" / "part_*" bodies and verify with
   checks (inside, no_overlap, min_distance).
8. Real parts: give board parts a STEP model (add_component model, e.g.
   KiCad kicad-packages3D or kiswitch for MX switches and hot-swap
   sockets) and import loose ones (switches, keycaps, dev boards); measure
   them before placing. Footprint holes (switch pins, pegs) are drilled.
    GND usually goes in pours on both layers plus stitch_vias.
9. Board artwork: set_board_style chooses mask (green, black, white, blue,
   red, purple, yellow) and white/black silkscreen ink. add_board_artwork
   prints text or a monochrome bitmap (# ink, . empty) on top/bottom;
   at is its center and width preserves aspect ratio. Bottom printing is
   mirrored automatically. update_board_artwork moves/resizes it;
   remove_board_artwork deletes it. get_board lists colors and artwork;
   render_board and render show it. run_drc checks custom ink against
   pads, board edges and holes, but fine ink lines/gaps still need DFM
   review. Gerbers carry the ink shapes; mask/ink colors are order
   preferences in export_manufacturing and must be selected explicitly
   with the manufacturer. This is single-color silk, not UV color printing.
10. Keep-outs before routing: add_keepout for antenna ends of radio
   modules (no tracks, vias, pours and parts, every layer), under crystals
   and inductors (no pours), and where a case boss or connector body sits
   (no parts). autoroute, pours and auto_place respect them; run_drc
   reports what is inside. set_board teardrops: true adds teardrops at
   pads and vias (derived copper: Gerber, DRC and pours include it).

## Editing print models (STL, 3MF)
- Files come from Import model in Ket, or from upload_asset: call it with
  the file name, then PUT the file to the upload link it returns (curl -T).
  list_assets gives their url (ket:asset/...) and a 3MF's objects;
  import url#<id> takes one object, where the slicer placed it.
- STL and 3MF become triangle-mesh bodies. measure them and section or
  render to find the walls, pockets and free space before changing them.
- section (axis, at) reads cuts as numbers: walls, pockets, free space.
  list_solids shows the separate pieces of a body; solids takes some of
  them (pick near a point, inBox, index, largest) without consuming the
  source, and with no pick makes a copy to use as a second input.
- Edit them with boolean: model the pocket, rib or label as B-rep (box,
  extrude of a sketch, text) and cut or union it. pattern and mirror
  repeat meshes; fillet, chamfer, shell and selectors need B-rep.
- Place a part by its box with transform align (to, anchor) instead of
  computing offsets: e.g. a piece lying in a pocket, bottom on the floor.
- Check with no_overlap / min_distance / inside as for any body.
- A body edited from a slicer project goes back into it with
  export_slicer_3mf (replace: [{ body, object: <its import> }]): print
  settings, plates and paint stay; new faces take the paint of nearby
  faces in the same plane. Say which objects changed and that the user
  should check the paint and re-slice. export 3mf/stl makes a plain file.
- arrange lays bodies flat on a plate (default 256 × 256) for printing.

## Enclosures that print and assemble
- One outline, many offsets: extrude the outline polygon, and its inside
  with profile inset: "wall" (lip: inset "lip_t", rebate: inset
  "lip_t + lip_c"). Never hand-offset points.
- Two shells: split at the board top; the base gets a lip around the
  outer wall, the top a matching rebate (0.15 mm clearance). Arms and
  legs locate with flat tongue-and-groove plates, not thin pins.
- Board screws from inside: pilot holes in bosses in the base; the top
  presses on the screw heads.
- Screws and inserts by size, not by hand-made cylinders: hole (plain,
  counterbore, countersink, tapped; size M2..M6, clearance 0.15 for
  printing) and insert_boss (heat-set inserts M2..M5) on a face picked by
  selector. thread only for M5 and up; smaller threads: tapped hole or
  insert. snap_fit hook + window for tool-free lids; draft for molded or
  cast parts. Two screws are enough for a small board:
  give the board tabs (sketch outline) into solid parts of the case, such
  as arms, and screw there, so the cavity under the board stays free for
  the battery.
- Every opening a user looks through or touches gets a closed part: a
  rounded-rect hole for USB-C sized to the connector shell + 0.2 mm, with
  the connector mouth flush with the outside wall (measure part_<REF>:
  a recessed port does not take a plug), closed windows for slide
  switches (knob + travel), a closed well for keys.
- Light: a clear cap seated flush in the top of the opening (seat 0.4 mm
  wider than the opening) with a hood around the LED so light does not
  bleed; not a solid block down to the board. Status LEDs of a dev board
  get a clear window in the wall next to them; a clear bezel can frame a
  port and cover its LEDs as one part. Cut openings after the fillet so
  their edges stay sharp.
- It must print: no strip of wall thinner than about 1.2 mm between an
  opening and an edge or the split (extend the opening to the edge
  instead); ribs, tongues and blocks join the walls on every side they
  reach (overlap them 0.3 mm into the wall), never stand free with a gap
  beside them. A union that leaves separate solids says so: fix it.
  Make it a check: min_wall (min 1.2) on each printed shell, and overhang
  (angle 45, axis = how it lies on the plate) so supports are a decision,
  not a surprise; min_wall samples, so read it as a strong hint.
- Openings at the split must be cut from both shells.
- Check: no_overlap between shells, every part against both shells,
  min_distance for moving parts (keycaps, buttons). measure_between
  lists where two bodies clash (boxes of each overlap piece).
- set_explode for an exploded view; render with explode: 1.
- The same part more than once (feet, hinges, two identical shells):
  model it once, then instance it with translate/rotate. Each instance is
  its own body (checks, explode, joints, STEP product) and follows the
  source. pattern instead when the copies should be one merged body.

## Rules of thumb
- Save editable source with export_project (.ket); open it in another empty
  project with import_project. Prepared footprints/routes travel with it,
  but remote models/textures still need network access. STEP/STL are
  geometry backups, not replacements for the editable project.
- Name features by purpose: case_body, usb_cutout, standoff_pattern.
- A feature's inputs are consumed: after a cut only the result is a body.
- To change a feature, use update_feature (a few fields) or the feature
  command with replace: true; everything downstream rebuilds.
- Selectors pick faces/edges by meaning (">Z" top, "|Z" vertical edges).
  Check them with list_faces / list_edges when unsure.
- Make cutting tools overlap the material they cut by at least 0.5 mm on
  each open side, and avoid coplanar faces between tool and target.
- Prefer one shell over many cuts for enclosures; add clearance (0.2-0.5 mm)
  for parts that must fit together when 3D printed.
- Variants of one design (board sizes, a bigger battery): keep one model
  and add set_configuration per variant with the parameter values that
  differ; use_configuration switches the built design, run_checks
  configurations: "all" verifies every variant, export / export_fab take
  configuration. Do not copy features per variant.
- Drawings for a workshop or a datasheet: drawing (front, top, right, iso
  with hidden lines and overall dimensions; SVG, PDF or DXF). Flat parts
  for a laser: export_dxf of the sketch, or of a body's face.
- If a command fails, read the message: it says what to change.

commands.name: set_parameters
commands.description: Create or update named parameters. Values are numbers (mm, degrees) or expressions over other parameters. Use parameters for every dimension that matters (board size, wall, clearance) so the design stays editable: change one and every feature that uses it rebuilds.

expr.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

commands.name: delete_parameters
commands.description: Delete parameters. Fails while a parameter, feature or check still uses one of them.

commands.name: set_configuration
commands.description: Create or update a configuration: a named variant of the design whose values replace those of the base parameters (e.g. "esp32s3" with board_w 52, "esp32c3" with board_w 40). Only existing parameters can be overridden; values are numbers or expressions like any parameter. Merges into an existing configuration with this name (pass replace: true to start it over). The design keeps building with the base parameters until use_configuration picks one. Verify every variant with run_checks configurations: "all".

additionalProperties.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

values.description: Parameter name → value in this configuration

replace.description: Replace the configuration instead of merging into it

commands.name: use_configuration
commands.description: Build the design with a configuration (its values replace the base parameters), or with the base parameters when name is omitted. Everything rebuilds: features, the board, checks. Exports use it too.

name.description: Configuration name; omit for the base parameters

commands.name: delete_configurations
commands.description: Delete configurations. When the active one goes, the design builds with the base parameters again.

commands.name: gear
commands.description: Add an involute gear: spur, helical, herringbone, internal (ring), rack, worm or bevel. Size: module (tooth size; pitch diameter = module × teeth) and teeth; width is the face width along the axis. Place the first gear of a train with center, axis and rotation; every other gear uses mesh: { with: "<earlier gear>", angle } (angle in degrees around the partner, or toward [x,y,z]) and gets its center, axis, hand and tooth phase solved so the teeth interlock, or coaxial: { with, offset } to share a shaft (compound trains). Then the whole train turns from one parameter: make the first gear's rotation an expression (e.g. "crank") and change it. Worm: teeth = starts, length, diameter; its wheel meshes with it as kind "helical" and gets the lead angle as helix. Bevel: pair_teeth = teeth of its mate (90° shafts; teeth are tapered involutes, fine for prints and models). Rack: length, meshes with a spur gear and slides. Optional: bore, hub, shaft, lightening holes, profile_shift for few teeth, backlash. get_gears lists ratios and diameters.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Bring in a real 3D model as a solid body you can place, check (inside, no_overlap, min_distance) and cut with. STEP (vendor or library model: a switch, a keycap, a dev board) becomes a B-rep solid. STL and 3MF (a print model, a slicer project) become a triangle-mesh body: boolean (union/cut/intersect with any body), transform, pattern, mirror, checks, measure and STL/3MF export work on it even at hundreds of thousands of triangles; fillet, chamfer, shell and face/edge selectors need B-rep bodies, so make cutting tools with box/extrude/sketch and cut them out of the mesh. url is an uploaded file ("ket:asset/<id>/<file>", from the Import model button in the UI; list them with list_assets) or https on an open model library: raw.githubusercontent.com (e.g. kiswitch/kiswitch for Cherry MX switches and Kailh hot-swap sockets, anhthang/dsa-keycap for keycaps, adafruit/Adafruit_CAD_Parts), gitlab.com (KiCad kicad-packages3D) or a vendor (files.seeedstudio.com). For a zip add #<file> to pick the model inside; for a 3MF with several objects add #<object id> or #<object name> (list_assets shows them). The model keeps its own origin and orientation (a 3MF object stays where the slicer placed it on the plate): measure it, then rotate (applied first) and translate it into place; scale converts units (0.0254 for inches... rarely needed).

Points are starting guesses; constraints hold the intent and the solver moves the points. Lines and arcs that share points form closed outlines; loops inside loops become holes. commands.description: Add a belt or chain loop around pulleys in a plane (plane coordinates as in sketch, offset = the plane's mid-belt position). Each pulley: at (center), d (pitch diameter) or teeth with the belt pitch (d = pitch / sin(180°/teeth), GT2 pitch 2, #25 chain 6.35). anyOf.description: A real 3D model for the part body (replaces the courtyard block part_<ref>): e.g. kiswitch MX switch or hot-swap STEP, a dev board STEP. Placed in footprint coordinates, then follows the part (side, rotation, position). Check it with render and measure part_<ref>.

dnp.description: Do not populate (left out of the BOM and CPL)

unroute.description: Remove the tracks and vias of the nets of parts that changed place (default false)

commands.name: auto_place
commands.description: Place parts automatically where their connections are shortest: parts go one by one (most connected first) to the free spot inside the board with no courtyard overlap that minimises their ratsnest, trying 0/90/180/270° (rotations to restrict), then improvement passes move and swap them. Edge connectors (edge: true) and parts in keep stay; with refs only those are placed. Connect nets first, put connectors and mounting holes where they must be, then auto_place, then autoroute. The result is ordinary positions: move_component to adjust. It also says the total ratsnest length before and after.

refs.description: Only these parts (default all except edge connectors)

unroute.description: Remove the tracks and vias of moved parts (default true; they no longer fit)

commands.name: remove_components
commands.description: Remove parts; their pins leave every net.

commands.name: connect
commands.description: Connect pins into named nets. Pins are REF.PIN with the pad number or the pin name from the part ("U1.3", "U1.VIN", "J1.GND"; a name on several pads takes all of them). Existing nets with the same name are extended. A pin already on another net is moved to this one. Connect everything before placing and routing.

commands.name: disconnect
commands.description: Remove pins from their nets, or delete whole nets by name.

commands.name: wire_pins
commands.description: Wire pins together, as drawing a wire on the schematic does. Pins on no net form a new net (named net, or N1, N2…); a pin joins the net of the others; pins on different nets merge them into one (the given name, else the first name that is not an automatic N…), and the copper of merged nets follows. Prefer connect when you know the net names.

pins.description: REF.PIN, e.g. ["U1.VOUT", "C2.1"]; drawn as a chain of wires

points.description: Bend points of the wire (two pins only), schematic units

commands.name: remove_wires
commands.description: Remove schematic wires (each given by its two pins, in any order). On an automatic net (N1, N2…) this also cuts the connection: the pins split into the groups the remaining wires join, and a pin left alone leaves the net. On a named net only the drawing goes; use disconnect to cut it.

commands.name: rename_net
commands.description: Rename a net (and its tracks, vias and pours). Renaming onto an existing net merges the two.

commands.name: set_net_class
commands.description: Create or change a net class: track width, clearance and via size for its nets (e.g. "power": 0.5 mm tracks). The "default" class applies to every other net.

commands.name: add_track
commands.description: Draw a track by hand: a polyline on one copper layer for a net. Width defaults to the net class. Usually autoroute does this; use add_track for short fixes.

commands.name: add_via
commands.description: Add a via for a net at [x, y]; size defaults to the net class.

commands.name: stitch_vias
commands.description: Stitch a net's copper pours together with vias: on a grid (pitch, default 5 mm) wherever the net's fill is on two or more layers, keeping clearance to other nets, pads, holes and existing vias. Use after add_zone on F.Cu and B.Cu (usually GND), so the two pours become one ground and pads that only one layer reaches join the net. Replaces earlier stitching vias of the net. Check with get_board (routing) and run_drc.

commands.name: unroute
commands.description: Remove tracks and vias: of the listed nets, or all of them.

commands.name: add_zone
commands.description: Add a copper pour for a net on a layer, usually GND on B.Cu (and/or F.Cu). Without polygon it covers the whole board. The fill keeps clearance to other nets, ties same-net pads with thermal spokes and drops islands that reach no pad of the net. Add pours after placing parts; autoroute routes the other nets and leaves the pour net to the pour, so add GND vias next to F.Cu GND pads when pouring only on B.Cu.

polygon.description: Board coordinates; default the whole board

clearance.description: To other nets; default the net class clearance

commands.name: add_keepout
commands.description: Mark an area of the board where tracks, vias, pours and/or parts may not go: the antenna end of an ESP32 module (no copper on any layer under and beside it), under a crystal or a switching inductor (no pours), the area a connector body or a mounting screw head covers (no parts). Give the polygon (board coordinates) or rect: { at, w, h } (center), the layers it applies to (default all; parts follow the side: F.Cu top, B.Cu bottom), and what it forbids. autoroute routes around it, pours leave it empty, auto_place keeps parts out and run_drc reports anything inside. Replaces a keep-out with the same name.

commands.name: remove_keepouts
commands.description: Remove keep-out areas by name.

commands.name: remove_mounting_holes
commands.description: Remove mounting holes by number (1-based, in the order get_board lists the board holes; part holes like hot-swap pins belong to their part), or all of them.

commands.name: remove_zones
commands.description: Remove copper pours by number (1-based, as get_board lists them), or all of a net.

commands.name: add_mounting_hole
commands.description: Add non-plated mounting holes (e.g. d 2.7 for M2.5 screws). Use the same parameters as the enclosure standoffs so they line up.

prefixItems.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"
Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

d.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

commands.name: autoroute
commands.description: Route the board with Ket's autorouter (runs in the browser): every net with 2+ pins. Tracks are 0/45/90° only, leave pads along their long side, keep each net class's width and clearance (power nets wide; they neck down only to reach fine-pitch pads) and use few vias; crowded nets are rerouted until they fit. Nets poured on every layer are left to the pour. Without nets/region it keeps existing copper and adds to it; with nets (or region) it reroutes just those: their old tracks and vias are replaced, everything else stays as an obstacle. Use it for "redo this part of the board": e.g. the user points at an area, pass region. Takes seconds. Then run_drc. If it fails or nets stay unrouted, give parts more room, move connectors to the edge or use 4 layers.

region.description: A box [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] on the board, mm: the nets with copper or pads in it

commands.name: tidy_tracks
commands.description: Clean up existing tracks without rerouting: straighten them (drop wiggles, stair steps and tiny back-and-forth segments, pulling each track tight while it keeps clearance to other copper and the board edge) and widen them to their net class width where it fits. Optionally set a new width first (e.g. "make GND thicker": nets ["GND"], width 0.6, or set_net_class). Limit it with nets or region; default all tracks. Connections stay as they are; run_drc after.

region.description: A box [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] on the board, mm: the nets with copper or pads in it

width.description: New width for these nets, mm: they move to a net class of that width; where it does not fit the track is as wide as fits

commands.name: get_board
commands.description: Read the board: outline size, solder-mask/silkscreen colors, printed artwork, parts (ref, part, package, position, rotation, side, size), nets with their pins (and pin names), routing status and copper counts.

commands.name: run_drc
commands.description: Design rule check against JLCPCB's standard capabilities: parts inside the outline and not overlapping, track width, clearance and shorts between nets, copper to edge, drills and hole spacing, printed artwork to exposed pads/edges/holes, plus unrouted nets. Each violation names the objects and the measured value. Fine artwork details still need manufacturer DFM review.

commands.name: render_board
commands.description: Draw the board from above (or below): outline, pads, tracks (top red, bottom blue), vias, refs, ratsnest lines for missing connections and red markers at DRC violations. highlight draws parts or nets in orange.

commands.name: export_fab
commands.description: Write the fabrication ZIP: Gerber X2 copper/mask/silk/outline, separate PTH and NPTH Excellon drill files (including rotated G85 slots), BOM and CPL. Refuses while DRC fails or nets are unrouted unless force is true. A history recovery failure cannot be bypassed.

configuration.description: Write the board of this configuration instead of the active design

commands.name: check_bom
commands.description: Check the bill of materials for an order of boards: per part the quantity, LCSC stock, unit price and line cost (rounded up to LCSC minimum/step), JLCPCB basic or extended (extended parts add a $3 setup fee each), and problems: out of stock, not enough stock for the order, parts without an LCSC number. Prices are refreshed when older than a day. Use it before export_fab, and to pick cheaper or basic alternatives (find_parts).

boards.description: Number of boards to build, default 5

commands.name: render_schematic
commands.description: Draw the schematic: every part's symbol with its pin names, wires where they were drawn (wire_pins) and a net label on connected pins a wire does not fully show (pins with the same label are connected). It is generated from the netlist, so it always matches the board. Use it to review the circuit: unconnected pins have no wire and no label.

commands.name: place_symbol
commands.description: Move symbols on the schematic (grid units of 10 mil; the auto layout is used for parts without a position). Purely visual: nets do not change.

commands.name: set_board_style

Verify with get_board or render_board. Match the choices in the manufacturer order form; actual colors and availability vary.

commands.name: add_board_artwork

Dark image pixels become ink regardless of ink color. Text uses the bundled IBM Plex Mono outline font. Artwork goes into 2D, 3D and Gerber, not copper. Use run_drc to check pad/edge clearance and render_board to inspect. Review fine details with the manufacturer. Prepared polygons are stored for deterministic replay and portable .ket files.

commands.name: set_pin_rules
commands.description: Declare electrical intent from datasheets, never by guessing names: input/output/bidirectional/passive/power_in/power_out/open_drain/no_connect and whether a connection is required. Pin accepts REF.pad or REF.name (all matching pads). null clears an annotation. No-connect cannot also be required. Verify with run_erc and get_problems. commands.name: run_erc
commands.description: Electrical rule check using explicit pin types: conflicting push-pull outputs/power sources, connected no-connect pins, required but unconnected pins, stale/multiply assigned pads, and unverified drivers. Returns severity, objects and actionable fixes plus typed/unknown coverage. Unknown types are not treated as passive. Does not certify voltage/current/analog behavior; use set_pin_rules from datasheets first.

commands.name: get_copper
commands.description: Read exact editable tracks and vias with their current 1-based numbers (the same object names used by get_problems). Filter by net/numbers and page results. Numbers are positions in the current revision, not permanent IDs: re-read after deleting/rerouting. Use edit_copper for small repairs, preview_changes before applying, then run_drc.

commands.name: edit_copper
commands.description: Precisely repair existing copper without rerouting whole nets: move/resize track segments or vias and/or remove numbered objects. Numbers are 1-based from the current get_copper/get_problems revision; all edits/removals reference the original arrays and are atomic. Net identity stays unchanged. Refuses conflicting/unknown numbers. Use preview_changes first and run_drc afterwards; this command does not certify legality or silently weaken rules.

commands.name: manufacturing_quote
commands.description: Check a board for manufacturer handoff: current DRC, unrouted nets, CAD checks, board dimensions, parts without real 3D models, and the official quote/API links for JLCPCB or PCBWay. Local preflight only: does not upload files, fetch a price, create an order or pay. Use export_manufacturing for the ZIP.

commands.name: export_manufacturing
commands.description: Download a prototype manufacturer handoff ZIP: Gerbers, drill, JLCPCB-style BOM/CPL, a machine-readable preflight/specification and ordering instructions. JLCPCB or PCBWay. Blocks on DRC, unrouted nets, failed geometry or failed checks; no force bypass. Does not upload/order/pay. Actual component fit and assembly rotations still need human review.

commands.name: cancel_operation
commands.description: Interrupt the current local kernel work and queued commands by restarting the executor, then rebuild the saved design. Runs outside the normal command queue, so it can stop a stuck build/router. Does not undo already-saved operations, cancel another agent conversation or abort remote provider requests. If a network preparation later completes, it is prevented from committing. Inspect get_document/get_problems afterwards; simpler geometry may be needed.

commands.name: get_problems
commands.description: One structured preflight for AI repair: history recovery, CAD build/requirements, PCB DRC and unrouted nets, explicit-pin ERC, manufacturing warnings. Stable IDs, severity, affected objects, XY locations, measured/required values where available, fix guidance and suggested commands. Filter/page results; counts always describe the whole design. Never auto-fixes or relaxes requirements. Re-run after each repair and render affected objects.

commands.name: focus_problem
commands.description: Show a current get_problems item to the user: selects its object and switches to PCB/3D with its location highlighted. Display-only, no design change or undo step. Refuses an obsolete problem ID; re-run get_problems after repairs.

commands.name: get_history
commands.description: Inspect the stored applied operation log and any replay recovery failure without changing it. Summary by default; detail full returns prepared arguments (can be large). Useful for diagnosing failed replay, reviewing AI edits and choosing how far to undo. No credentials/server identities. Requires an open project session.

commands.name: preview_changes
commands.description: Dry-run an atomic batch against the current design without committing anything. Prepares each step against preceding steps, builds the candidate and compares unified get_problems before/after: introduced and resolved IDs, remaining errors, change summary. Does not upload, save, export, auto-apply or weaken checks. If acceptable, apply the same steps with batch (or work on a proposal). Expensive geometry/routing still runs; only the design commit is suppressed.

commands.name: export_project
commands.description: Save an editable .ket project (versioned JSON with prepared operations): parameters, sketches, CAD, PCB, materials, checks and routing. Open it in another empty project with import_project or the Import Ket button. Does not include users, credentials or server IDs. Remote models/textures remain URL references and require network access. Unlike STL/STEP it preserves the editable design.

commands.name: import_project
commands.description: Open the contents of a .ket project file in this project. Atomic, undoable and deterministic; never downloads or routes during replay. Refuses to replace a nonempty design unless replace: true. File is JSON format ket-project version 1; use export_project to create it. External assets are fetched by the normal build pipeline.

data.description: The entire JSON text of a .ket project file

replace.description: Explicitly replace the current design (default false)
